chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Durays ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves cooling the hot liver (of the thirsty), and whoever gives a drink to a hot liver from an animal or from another source, Allah will shade him on the Day when there is no shade except His Shade.

key_terms.إِبْرَادَ الْكَبِدِ: Cooling the liver (metaphor for quenching thirst)
key_terms.يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلُّهُ: The Day when there is no shade except His Shade

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for giving drinks to the thirsty according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing the spiritual merit of 'ibrad al-kabid' (cooling the hot liver) as a tangible act of mercy. This tradition underscores the universality of charity in Shia ethics, extending divine favor to those who quench the thirst of both humans and animals, thereby securing Allah's shade on the Day of Resurrection when no other shade exists.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zureys Bin Abdul Malik, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Loves cooling the hot liver (a thirsty one), and the one who quenches a hot liver from an animal, or something else, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Shade him on a Day in which there would be no shade except for His<sup>azwj</sup> Shade’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Durays ibn ‘Abd al-Malik who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Allah, the most Blessed, the most High, loves cooling off a thirsty liver. Whoever cools off a thirsty liver of an animal or others, Allah on the Day of Judgment provides him a shadow when there is no shadow except His shadow.”
